findings.reason: Confirmed. GH.0/the-variety-X-r-and-its-smooth-proper-model states that X_r 'admits a PROPER SMOOTH MODEL over Spec Z[1/N]', and its hypothesis 2 makes 'p does not divide N' the certificate of good reduction and of H^1_f. BDP's introduction (p.1035) does say this verbatim, but the paper's own definitions do not support it. §2.2 (p.1060) defines X_r := W_r × A^r over a field F ⊇ H, with A a CM curve over the Hilbert class field H (§1.4, no reduction condition). The appendix (p.1139, read through p.1144) constructs only the compactified Kuga–Sato factor W_r over Z[1/N] and never mentions A or X_r. §3.2 (p.1067) applies Faltings' comparison under two explicit assumptions: F finite unramified over Q_p, and C, X_r have smooth proper models over O_F. The introduction's own H^1_f statement (p.1040) also assumes p ∤ level, d_K and deg φ. The counterexample holds: a quadratic twist of A by a character of G_H ramified at a good prime keeps CM by O_K over H but has additive reduction there, and H^1(A) is a Künneth summand of H^1(X_r) for r ≥ 1 (e.g. K=Q(i), N=5, p=13, y² = x³ − 169x). The fix is right, with these additions. (i) Correct every occurrence: the node title, statement, hypotheses 2–3, proof steps 2–3, acceptance 2, the p.1035 'match' line, the GH.0→GH.1 link reason, the GH.0 review verdict and note, the packet summary and the GH.0 coverage record. (ii) Make good reduction of A above p an explicit supplied hypothesis (A extends to an elliptic scheme over O_F), and record p ∤ cNd_K only as BDP's application condition for their chosen A; the 13-twist also satisfies p ∤ cNd_K, so neither condition certifies good reduction. (iii) Keep the appendix attribution for W_r over Z[1/N] and form W_r⊗O_F × 𝒜^r from the supplied model. (iv) Cite p.1040's hypotheses beside §3.2's.

Confirmed on the page image of Kato, printed p.182: '(8.4.1) T_pE ≅ H¹_p(1) … induces (8.4.2) Sym^{k−2}(H¹_p) ≅ (Sym^{k−2}(T_pE))(2 − k)', and the composite (8.4.3) goes from Sym^{k−2}(T_pE/pⁿ)(2 − r) to Sym^{k−2}(H¹_p)/pⁿ(k − r). The node L1/etale-chern-moment-map-into-modular-local-system writes 'Sym^{k-2}(T_pE) = Sym^{k-2}(H_p)(2-k)', which contradicts its own T = H(1) unless k = 2. Applied to step (ii) it gives twist 4−k−r instead of k−r; at k=4, r=1 that is −1 instead of 3. A weight-two test hides the error. The fix is right: Sym(T) ≅ Sym(H)(k−2), or Kato's orientation. The occurrence list must include the statement step (iii), proofSteps[2] and the sources[2] excerpt, which misquotes Kato and should be restored verbatim. Reword hypotheses[2], sources[2].match and review.checked[7]. The same text is copied in research/expansion/external/EXT-15/KatoEulerSystems.json and the generated naming files (planets-current.json, PLANETS-12.json, index.html), which should be regenerated.

Confirmed on the page images. §9.2 (printed p.187) defines a descending filtration D^i_dR(V) = H⁰(K, B^i_dR ⊗ V), and (9.2.2) reads 'D^i_dR(V) = D_dR(V) for i ≤ 0, D^i_dR(V) = 0 for i ≥ k, D^i_dR(V) = M_k(X) ⊗ Q_p for 1 ≤ i ≤ k−1'. §9.4 (p.188): 'D⁰_dR(V(i)) = D^i_dR(V) = M_k(X) ⊗ Q_p'. The node L3/dual-exponential-map-on-the-modular-local-system instead calls this 'the graded piece in degrees 1 ≤ i ≤ k−1' and writes 'D^i = 0 for i > k'. Its excerpt misquotes the endpoint. Since the filtration is constant on 1 ≤ i ≤ k−1, gr^i = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ k−2, so for k ≥ 3 the stated target is zero at every r ≥ 2 (e.g. k=3, r=2); this is a wrong target type, not wording. The fix is right. The complete edit list is: the statement (phrase and endpoint), hypotheses[2], acceptance[0] and [1] (the target is the filtration step S(f)⊗F_λ), sources[1].excerpt ('i ≥ k'), the reciprocity node's acceptance[2], review.checked[13] and the EXT-15 and generated copies. Add the interior-degree F^i-versus-gr^i test and an i = k test.

Confirmed on the page image of Thm 12.5(1) (printed p.221): 'H¹(V_{F_λ}(f)) ≃ H¹(V_{F_λ}(f)(k−r)) → H¹(Q_p(ζ_{p^n}), V_{F_λ}(f)(k−r)) —exp*→ S(f) ⊗ … (the first isomorphism is the product with (ζ_{p^n})^{⊗(k−r)}_{n≥1})'. The node L3/zeta-class-interpolation-of-complex-L-values restricts first and then multiplies by the roots of unity to the power −r. Its own source excerpt is correct, so the statement contradicts it. The error is also a type error. By §9.4, F⁰D_dR(V_f(−r)) = D_dR(V_f), the whole 2-dimensional space, not S(f)⊗F_λ; only i = k−r lies in the range 1 ≤ i ≤ k−1 where exp*_f lands in S(f), consistent with Thm 9.5. The twist also cannot be applied after restriction at level n, because H¹(Q_p(ζ_{p^n}), V) and H¹(Q_p(ζ_{p^n}), V(j)) differ for j ≠ 0. The fix is right: twist on Iwasawa cohomology by ∪(ζ_{p^n})^{⊗(k−r)} (Λ-semilinear), then specialize, localize and apply exp*_f with i = k−r. The target-type test should check that F⁰D_dR(V_f(k−r)) is 1-dimensional at k=2, r=1 while F⁰D_dR(V_f(−r)) is 2-dimensional. Update the review note. The stale L3 coverage remark that Thm 12.5(1)'s constant 'was not transcribed' can be cleaned up at the same time.

Confirmed on the page image of the proof of Lemma 8.5 (printed p.184). It identifies the cokernel with H⁰(Gal(K_v^ur/K_v), H¹(K_v^ur,T)) ≅ {H¹(F_v, H⁰(K_v^ur,T^∨(1)))}^∨, factors the composite through {lim→_n H¹(F_v(ζ_{p^n}), H⁰(K_v^ur,T^∨(1)))}^∨, and reduces to lim→ = 0 by p-cohomological dimension zero. The node L2/integrality-of-the-cyclotomic-limit-in-S-integral-cohomology instead writes H¹(Gal, H¹(I_v,T)) (the E₂^{1,1} term, which contributes to H² rather than to the H¹ cokernel), drops the dual, and replaces lim→ by lim←. The vanishing it asserts is in fact false under the natural maps. For T = μ_p and v ∤ p, H¹(F_v(ζ_{p^n}), Z/p) = Z/p with corestriction an isomorphism, so lim← = Z/p ≠ 0, while restriction is multiplication by p for large n, so lim→ = 0. The theorem statement itself is correct. The fix is right. Additions: correct the node's source excerpt, which also drops the direction ('lim_n' → lim→_n); write T^∨(1) for the undefined T^*(1); note that K_v(ζ_{p^n})/K_v is unramified since v ∤ p; update the review note; and add the μ_p regression test.

Confirmed on the page image of Kato §1.10 (printed p.124): 'the image of the divisor c²(0) − _cE under the multiplication a : E → E is c²(0) − _cE itself. Since the map a_* on Pic(E)^{deg=0} is compatible with the multiplication by a …'. The node L0/theta-function-c-normalised proof step 2 says 'because a^* fixes the divisor', which is false. With c=5, a=2: [2]^*D = 25E[2] − E[10], so a nonzero 2-torsion point has coefficient 24, not 0, whereas [2]_*D = D because [2] fixes 0 and permutes E[5]. This is the only occurrence. The node's own step 3 already uses div(N_a f) = a_* div f. The fix is right and complete: replace a^* by a_*, tie it to div(N_a f) = a_* div(f) and Abel's compatibility, and add the c=5, a=2 pullback countercheck. One nuance: on Pic⁰ ≅ E, [a]^* also corresponds to multiplication by a, so only the divisor identity is wrong, not the Pic compatibility. Over a general base S, say that a_*D = D because [a] fixes the zero section and restricts to an automorphism of the finite flat group scheme E[c] when (a,c) = 1.

Confirmed. PS.2's text (identical in content/campaign/PeriodsAndSpecialValues/README.md, research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/PeriodsAndSpecialValues.json and the data/atlas.json stage) constructs the formal periods from integration data with linearity, change of variables and Stokes, and proves the comparison with the Nori torsor. Its acceptance is 'Represent 2πi …'. Huber–Müller-Stach (arXiv:1105.0865v5, p.2, Def 0.1 and Thm 0.2) define P⁺ by exactly those relations and products, then 'The space of formal periods is the localization P of P⁺ with respect to the period of (G_m,{1},dX/X,S¹)'. The torsor theorem concerns Spec(P), and ev maps that symbol to 2πi (p.11). Without the localization the comparison fails: in the rank-one Tate case the effective algebra is Q[t] while the torsor ring is Q[t,t⁻¹]. No supplier stage names the localization. MC.4 is Voevodsky-style Tate stabilization; MC.5–MC.6 are the Nori diagram category, tensor/duality structures and torsors; MC.1 localizes Chow motives. Neither roadmap has a decomposition or packet, atlas-wide searches find no layer planning P = P⁺[L⁻¹], and the pinned libraries have no Nori or formal-period algebra. The fix is right. Additions: update all three copies consistently, including the acceptance line; state the comparison as HMS do (P⁺ ≅ A^eff_{1,2} by Thm 2.6, then localize both sides, P ≅ A_{1,2}); confirm that MC.5 exports the localized Nori diagram and category (HMS Def. B.18, Prop. B.22, Thm 1.6(3)) or add it to MC.5 as a supplier export, rather than planning it in PS.2; and add a negative test that the effective Tate algebra Q[t] is not a G_m-torsor ring.
